14 Two forces, each of magnitude F, act in opposite directions on a rod.

Each force acts on the rod at a distance d from the pivot P.
What is the torque of this couple about P?
A
0
B
F  d
C
2F  d
D
2F  2d

hints: Look at the diagram: the left $F$ acts upward a distance $d$ left of P and the right $F$ acts downward a distance $d$ right of P.
Recall torque about P is $F$ times perpendicular distance, and check whether each force would turn the rod clockwise or anticlockwise about P.
Add the two torque magnitudes with their signs: two equal torques in the same sense give twice $F \times d$, not zero and not a single $F \times d$.
walkthrough: Identify the given data from the diagram: two equal forces of magnitude $F$ in opposite directions, each with perpendicular distance $d$ from pivot P.
State the rule: torque about a point is $torque = F \times$ perpendicular distance, with clockwise taken as one sign and anticlockwise as the opposite sign.
Check the left force: $F$ upward to the left of P tends to rotate the rod clockwise, so its torque magnitude is $F \times d$ clockwise.
Check the right force: $F$ downward to the right of P also tends to rotate the rod clockwise, so its torque magnitude is also $F \times d$ clockwise.
Add them because they act in the same rotational sense: total torque $= F \times d + F \times d = 2F \times d$.

A.explanation: Net force is zero for this couple, but net torque is not zero because the two $F$ forces tend to turn the rod the same way.

B.explanation: This is the magnitude $F \times d$ from only one force about P; the second force on the other side adds an equal torque in the same rotational sense.

C.explanation: Each force gives torque $F \times d$ in the same clockwise sense about P, so total torque is $F \times d + F \times d = 2F \times d$.

D.explanation: The separation between the forces is $2d$, but torque is not $(2F) \times (2d)$; each $F$ is multiplied only by its own distance $d$ from P.
